Umbra has facilitated the transfer of more than $155 million worth of crypto assets across all chains where it is deployed.
Umbra is the second most popular privacy-enhancing technology used on Ethereum and its layer-2 systems after the AZTEC protocol.

The authors collected transaction data for stealth key registrations, Umbra sends and withdraws, and registrant, sender, and withdrawer transactions across the Ethereum mainnet, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Optimism networks.

The authors find that their heuristics can link the real recipients of 48.5%, 25.8%, 65.7%, and 52.6% of all Umbra transactions on the Ethereum mainnet, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Optimism networks, respectively.

The 'collector pattern' heuristic, where users withdraw multiple incoming stealth payments to a single address, greatly reduces the Shannon entropy of stealth payment recipients, from 13.36 bits to 8.86 bits on the Arbitrum network.

Umbra became more popular on Layer-2 solutions like Arbitrum, Optimism, and Polygon than on the Ethereum mainnet after the previous most popular on-chain privacy-enhancing technology, Tornado Cash, was banned in the U.S.
As of July 2023, there are nearly 70,000 registered users in the stealth key registries of Umbra across all chains.
